brief: Goldman Sachs daily note for 7 Sep 2026, a Labor Day session with NYSE closed and no major data. Stat of the day: VXSMH, a proxy for semiconductor implied volatility, has fallen from roughly 65 in July to 36, back toward where 2026 started, after a painful stretch for long-vol positions. Rates: global yields sit at or near recent highs because energy price risk limits sustainable relief, and since rates volatility has not risen with yields, the note argues non-fundamental drivers are hard to blame, so lasting relief requires a changed view on cyclical resilience, inflation, fiscal policy or AI debt supply. Fedspeak has restored the front-end as the primary US response point, leaving September pricing to next week's inflation news. Preference is 5s10s steepeners. European gas upside risks the European and UK front-ends, which shifts risk reward away from UK steepeners, while a hawkish BoJ reassessment drives JGB flattening, with front-end receives as an overlay. Research: Buy-rated TALO gets a raised $20 target, 16% upside, on a 13% FCF yield versus 10% for peers. VSXY beat 2Q and raised FY26 guidance, but reinvestment softens the 3Q profit outlook. Tesla's Cybercab launched, with 1 million unsupervised miles claimed.
